subject: Clarify deployment boundary & isolation requirements for pilot
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@clearharborhealth.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@clearharborhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & a few clarification asks re: isolation needs

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the specific items we need to determine next steps for a pilot: 

- What you told us: ClearHarbor needs strict data isolation for PHI-derived inference. You prefer a separate tenant with network-level separation and control-plane residency in your VPC if possible. You also listed BYOK for key material and a 90-day deletion policy for model inputs.

- Our ask / open questions:
  1) Do you require physical host tenancy (dedicated GPUs) or is a logically isolated Dedicated cluster sufficient provided the control plane and key management stay in your VPC?
  2) For the pilot, will you accept redacted PII / synthetic data, or do you want an initial scoped test with a minimal subset of real records?
  3) Any mandatory compliance artifacts we should bring to the workshop (SOC2 report, encryption evidence, network segmentation diagrams)?

Proposed next steps: we can schedule a breakout workshop with our infra/security SMEs to map the deployment options (Hosted API with enhanced controls vs Redwood Dedicated vs Private VPC). Can you share a preferred window next week?

Attachments: none on this message.

Thanks — looking forward to narrowing the path.

— Logan
Logan Wright | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@clearharborhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@clearharborhealth.com>, ClearHarbor Health Security <security@clearharborhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2026 09:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & a few clarification asks re: isolation needs

Thanks Logan — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Physical vs logical separation: for Phase 1 we would prefer private VPC control plane with Dedicated capacity in tenant-isolated hosts if possible. The goal is that production inference for any records classified as PHI runs on hardware that is not multi-tenant. If that is a hard blocker, we can discuss mitigations but it would be a strong preference.

- BYOK: required. Keys must live in our KMS and we need proof that the inference path never leaves the encrypted boundary unwrapped.

- Data retention: 90 days retention for inputs/kv-cache and automatic purge thereafter. 

- Pilot: we can start with a scoped dataset (10k records) with real PII under a DTA. For the first call I want to include our security lead (cc’d) to validate whether the pilot scope is acceptable.

Requested artifacts for the workshop: SOC2 Type II summary, any network segmentation/egress controls doc, and an example keystore/BYOK integration playbook. If you have a short ops checklist or runbook for Private VPC onboarding, please include.

I attached our rough network topology for the pilot (internal only).

Best — Sam
Samantha Liu | Head of Product Security
ClearHarbor Health
samantha.liu@clearharborhealth.com

Attachment: clearharbor_network_topology_v1.pdf (PDF)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@clearharborhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@clearharborhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & a few clarification asks re: isolation needs

On Tue, May 25, 2026 at 09:20 AM Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@clearharborhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Logan — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
> 
> - Physical vs logical separation: for Phase 1 we would prefer private VPC control plane with Dedicated capacity in tenant-isolated hosts if possible. The goal is that production inference for any records classified as PHI runs on hardware that is not multi-tenant. If that is a hard blocker, we can discuss mitigations but it would be a strong preference.

Thanks for the fast reply and for the topology PDF — that's helpful. 

To address each ask at a high level (we'll cover details in the workshop):
- Hardware tenancy: Redwood Private (customer VPC) is the only option that guarantees control-plane residency in your VPC and gives you the strong isolation you described. We can provision Dedicated GPU hosts inside that deployment, which meets your non-multi-tenant hardware requirement.
- BYOK: supported in Private via KMS integrations (we have a BYOK playbook). We'll provide an architecture diagram showing key wrapping and where keys are unwrapped (spoiler: only in your VPC).
- Retention & purge: we can enforce a 90-day TTL on inputs and have an auditable deletion flow; Marissa will include the audit log retention and purge confirmation steps in the workshop artifacts.
- Pilot scope: scoped real data for 10k records is fine under a DTA — we'll need an approved DTA and an Ops checklist (network allowlist, certs, SSH jumpbox rules as applicable).

Action items / next steps: 
1) Workshop: propose Wed 5/27 10:00–11:30 PT for an infra + security deep dive. Please confirm or propose alternate windows.
2) I'll attach our SOC2 summary and a condensed Private VPC onboarding checklist after I sync with Marissa.
3) Please share the signed DTA (or redlines) and the initial pilot dataset access plan.

Looping in Karthik (infra lead) and Marissa (security ops) to prepare the artifacts. Karthik / Marissa — can you confirm BYOK playbook readiness and whether we need to run any additional approvals for a Dedicated-hosts-in-Private deployment?

— Logan

Redwood Inference
